ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p161/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p161/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p161/r2.claim: Pharaoh turned away and plotted to defeat Moses by arranging a contest with Aaron and expert magicians; his advisers warned ordinary magicians risked defeat.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p161/r2.anchor: it would be better if expert magicians were called up from all parts of the empire

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r19.claim: Pharaoh rebelled against God and His command, spurning purification with the taunt “Who is the Lord of the worlds?”
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r19.anchor: temizlenmeye niyet etmek şöyle dursun وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ [eş-Şu‘arâ 26/23] “o Rabbü’l-âlemîn ne oluyormuş” diye karşılayarak inkâr ve isyâna cüret etti.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r20.claim: Pharaoh could not prevail in denial and rebellion, yet worked hard in the wrong direction, turning his back on God and heading toward destruction.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r20.anchor: tekzib ve isyanda muvaffak olamadı, bununla beraber boş da durmadı, koştu, çalıştı; lâkin ikbâle doğru çalışmadı, idbâra doğru çalıştı

QASHANI:79:18-26/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:18-26/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:18-26/r4.claim: Pharaoh turned away from the station of unity of attributes toward the station of the soul, driven by hostility and the soul’s dominance.
QASHANI:79:18-26/r4.anchor: ثم أدبر } عن مقام توحيد الصفات الذي هو فيه لذنب حاله وتوجه إلى مقام النفس بالكلية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r1.claim: Pharaoh denied that the two signs came from God, disobeyed, turned away from faith, and worked to spread corruption.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r1.anchor: فكذب} بأنهما من الله {وعصى} {ثم أدبر} تولى وأعرض عن الإيمان {يسعى} يعمل بالفساد في الأرض.

BINTSHATI:v1p146/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r2.claim: Here, turning away means turning from Moses and the great sign he showed.
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r2.anchor: والإدبار هنا هو الإعراض عن موسى وما أراه من الاية الكبرى.

BINTSHATI:v1p146/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r3.claim: In this emotional context, Pharaoh’s striving means confronting the danger and preventing people from believing Moses, not fleeing in panic.
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r3.anchor: والسعي لا يكون في هذا الجو النفسي - المروع بما سمع من النبي المرسل ورأى من آيته الكبرى - إلا لمواجهة الخطر والحيلولة دون تصديق الناس برسالة موسى.

BINTSHATI:v1p146/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r4.speaker: مفسرون
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r4.claim: The author rejects exegetes’ reading that Pharaoh turned away and hurried off in terror of the serpent, calling it an unsupported forced interpretation.
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r4.anchor: دون حاجة إلى تكلف في تأويل الإدبار هنا بأنه فرار فرعون مرعوباً من الحية، وأن السعي هو الإسراع في المشية عن ذعر وطيش

BINTSHATI:v1p146/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r5.claim: A serpent trick would not plausibly terrify Pharaoh in a culture familiar with magic and staged serpents.
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r5.anchor: لأن الذعر من رؤية الثعبان منقلباً عن عصا، يبدو لنا مستبعداً في بيئة كانت تمارس السحر وتأليف أفاعيل السحرة

BINTSHATI:v1p146/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r6.claim: The author invokes Pharaoh’s response to Moses’ staff before the magicians in Ta-Ha: the magicians submitted, while Pharaoh remained defiant and threatened them.
BINTSHATI:v1p146/r6.anchor: والقرآن نفسه يحدثنا في (سورة طه 57و 71) عن موقف فرعون حين حشر السحرة من قومه، فألقوا حبالهم وعصيهم.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r6.claim: After a delay and many major events, Pharaoh turned away and persisted in even greater tyranny.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r6.anchor: بعد المهلة والأناة إدبارا عظيما بالتمادي على أعظم مما كان فيه من الطغيان بعد خطوب جليلة ومشاهد طويلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r23.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r23.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r23.claim: Some exegetes take Pharaoh’s turning away and running literally: he left the place and fled Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r23.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: أدبر يسعى حقيقة قام من موضعه موليا فارا بنفسه عن مجالسة موسى عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r24.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r24.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r24.claim: Mujahid reads turning away as rejecting faith and running as striving against Moses’s cause and law.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r24.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أدبر كناية عن إعراضه عن الإيمان، ويسعى معناه:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r1.claim: Mujahid explains Pharaoh’s running as an effort to resolve Moses’s challenge and oppose his law.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r1.anchor: يتحذم حل أمر موسى عليه السلام والرد في وجه شرعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh turned away to confront truth with falsehood, gathering magicians to oppose Moses’ manifest miracle.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {ثم أدبر يسعى} أي: في مقابلة الحق بالباطل، وهو جمعه السحرة ليقابلوا ما جاء به موسى، عليه السلام، من المعجزة الباهرة

JISHUMI:v10p7268/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r9.claim: Idbār is the opposite of turning toward and literally derives from turning one's back; idiomatically it marks troubled affairs, while iqbāl marks affairs becoming sound and movement toward good.
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r9.anchor: والإدبار: نقيض الإقبال، والإدبار مأخوذ من تولية الدبر، ويقال: أدبر: إذا اضطربت عليه أموره

JISHUMI:v10p7271/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r10.claim: Jishumi argues that human acts originate from the servants themselves, citing Pharaoh's transgression, denial, turning away, and calling out.

MUQATIL:79:15-26/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r11.claim: Pharaoh turned away from truth and hurried to gather the magicians, as shown by the cited verse.
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r11.anchor: { ثم أدبر } عن الحق { يسعى } [آية: 22] يعني في جمع السحر فهو قوله:

NAHHAS:v5p143/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p143/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p143/r13.claim: يسعى is a circumstantial expression describing Pharaoh as he turns away.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r1.claim: He disbelieved in Moses, God's prophet, and disobeyed his Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r1.anchor: { فكذب } أي كذب نبي الله موسى { وعصى } أي عصى ربه عز وجل.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r2.claim: He turned away from faith and worked corruption in the land.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r2.anchor: ثم أدبر يسعى } أي ولى مدبرا معرضا عن الإيمان «يسعى» أي يعمل بالفساد في الأرض.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r3.claim: Another explanation says Pharaoh worked to harm Moses.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r4.claim: Another explanation says he fled from the serpent.

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r12.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r12.claim: One view says Pharaoh turned and fled upon seeing the greatest sign or the staff become a serpent.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r12.anchor: Some say that this verse indicates that Pharaoh turned and fled when he saw the greatest sign or the staff turned serpent (R).

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r13.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r13.claim: Another view says Pharaoh quickly devised a plan against Moses after recognizing the power of his message.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r13.anchor: Others say it indicates that, upon realizing the power of Moses’ message, Pharaoh quickly moved to devise a plan against him (R).

TABRISI:79:15-24/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:15-24/r18.claim: Pharaoh turned away to find something that could defeat Moses' great proof, but only increased in error.
TABRISI:79:15-24/r18.anchor: { ثم أدبر } فرعون أي ولى الدبر ليطلب ما يكسر به حجة موسى في المعجزة العظيمة

TABRISI:79:15-24/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r19.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:79:15-24/r19.claim: Al-Jubba'i says Pharaoh fled after seeing the huge serpent because he was afraid of it.
TABRISI:79:15-24/r19.anchor: لما رأى الحية في عظمها خاف منها فأدبر وسعى هربا عن الجبائي

TABRISI:79:15-24/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:15-24/r20.claim: The word yas'a means that Pharaoh worked corruption in the land.
TABRISI:79:15-24/r20.anchor: { يسعى } أي يعمل بالفساد في الأرض

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r3.claim: Pharaoh then turned away and worked corruption in the land.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r3.anchor: ثم أدبر } أعرض عنه { يسعى } في الأرض يعمل فيها بالفساد.

TAB-FULL:v24p83/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p83/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p83/r1.claim: Pharaoh turned away from Moses’ call to obey, fear, and affirm God’s oneness, then worked at disobeying God and doing what angers Him.
TAB-FULL:v24p83/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ثم أدبر يسعى} [النازعات: 22] قال: يعمل بالفساد

TAB-FULL:v24p83/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p83/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p83/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses his striving as working corruption.
TAB-FULL:v24p83/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ثم أدبر يسعى} [النازعات: 22] قال: يعمل بالفساد

TABATABAI:79:19-22/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r9.claim: Idbār means turning away, and saʿy means energetic striving; Pharaoh turned away and worked hard to undo Moses' mission and oppose him.
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r9.anchor: الإدبار التولي والسعي هو الجد والاجتهاد أي ثم تولى فرعون يجد ويجتهد في إبطال أمر موسى ومعارضته

BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r9.claim: Pharaoh then turned away from obedience and from speaking with Moses; ثم marks a time interval because trying to undo Moses’ mission required time.
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r9.anchor: أي تولى عن الطاعة وكلمه ثم على هذا معناها التراخي الزماني إذا السعي في إبطال أمره يقتضي مهلة

BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p249#2/r10.claim: Alternatively, أدبر means that Pharaoh left the gathering.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#4/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#4/r1.claim: Pharaoh turned away from truth and faith and set about spreading corruption in the land.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#4/r1.anchor: أعرض عن الحق، والإيمان (¬7). {يسعى} يعمل بالفساد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r10.claim: One view takes أدبر literally: Pharaoh got up and fled for his life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r10.anchor: قيل: أدبر حقيقة، أي قام من مكانه فارا بنفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r11.claim: The majority take أدبر figuratively as turning away from faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r11.anchor: وقال الجمهور: هو كناية عن إعراضه عن الإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r12.claim: Pharaoh exerted himself in struggling against Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r12.anchor: يسعى: يجتهد في مكابدة موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh turned from obedience and strove to thwart Moses and oppose the sign; alternatively, he literally left the gathering to work against it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r1.anchor: تولى عن الطاعة يسعى أي ساعيا مجتهدا في إبطال أمره عليه السلام ومعارضة الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r2.claim: The sequence ثم can indicate the long time needed to undo Moses’ mission.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r2.anchor: وثم لأن إبطال ذلك ونقضه يقتضي زمانا طويلا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r3.speaker: بعض الآثار
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r3.claim: One account says Pharaoh fled when Moses’ staff became a huge, open-mouthed serpent; Pharaoh defecated, the crowd stampeded, and 25,000 people died.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r3.anchor: وقيل أدبر يسعى هاربا من الثعبان فإنه روي أنه لما ألقى العصا انقلبت ثعبانا أشعر فاغرا فاه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r4.speaker: بعض الآثار
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r4.claim: Another report says the serpent rose a mile, threatened Pharaoh at Moses’ command, then returned to a staff when Moses took it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r4.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أنها انقلبت حية وارتفعت في السماء قدر ميل ثم انحطت مقبلة نحو فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r5.claim: Alusi says the fleeing-serpent account does not fit if this comes after the customary gathering of magicians; if before it, the delay signaled by ثم is unclear. It may instead stress how startling his frightened flight was, or use أدبر ironically for ‘began’, signaling ruin.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#2/r5.anchor: أن هذا إن كان بعد حشر السحرة للمعارضة كما هو المشهور فلا تظهر صحة إرادته ههنا إذا أريد بالحشر بعد حشرهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r9.claim: He turned from obedience and strove to undo Moses's mission, or fled in terror after seeing the serpent.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r9.anchor: عن الطاعة. { يسعى } ساعيا في إبطال أمره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r7.claim: Thumma marks a higher escalation in purpose: Pharaoh moves from denial and disobedience to turning away, hurrying to suppress the call, and claiming divinity after considering the danger that it might spread.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r7.anchor: وعطف { ثم أدبر يسعى } ب { ثم } للدلالة على التراخي الرتبي كما هو شأنها في عطف الجمل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh turned away from faith and worked to spread corruption in the land.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#2/r1.anchor: ثم أدبر أي أعرض عن الإيمان يسعى أي يعمل بالفساد في الأرض

MUJAHID:v2p727#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p727#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p727#3/r1.claim: Mujahid construes Pharaoh's striving as seeking corruption, as in 5:33, and rejects the sense of physically running.
MUJAHID:v2p727#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ ثم أدبر يسعى ﴾ قال يقول يسعى بالفساد كقوله ﴿ ويسعون في الأرض فسادا ﴾ وليس هو الشد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#13/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#13/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#13/r2.claim: One explanation is that Pharaoh strove to plot against Moses.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#13/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#13/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#13/r3.claim: Alternatively, on seeing the serpent he fled in terror, hurrying along because he was rash and impulsive.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#13/r3.anchor: لما راى الثعبان أدبر مرعوبا يسرع فى مشيته وكان طياشا خفيفا
